Chief Executive’s Foreword 
 
 
Last month, Fingal County Council reached a major 
sustainability milestone with confirmation that the use 
of one million plastic bottles was avoided with EcoFil water 
dispensing stations across the county. The water stations are 
in place in thirty-one locations with three high use locations 
saving over 90,000 plastic bottles each. Fingal is the first local 
authority in Ireland to achieve the milestone and it speaks to 
the commitment of the people of the county to build upon 
positive sustainability practices and to engage with initiatives 
which provide reusable options and seek to reduce waste. The 
Ecofil Iconic-V water dispensers were developed and 
manufactured in Ireland and since their launch in 2023, they 
have proven to be sturdy, weather resistant and hygienic 
sources of refreshing water for sports teams, walkers/joggers 
and visitors to our parks and public realm spaces. I am pleased 
that our installations have proven so convenient and popular, 
whether you are out for a walk or supporting your team in a 
local park or even enjoying the beach on a sunny afternoon, 
please take the opportunity to fill up at your nearest Ecofil 
dispenser listed  
here:   Water Stations in Fingal  
 
The town of Balbriggan is undergoing a significant 
rejuvenation at the moment with works continuing on 
delivering economic, infrastructural and social features of the 
Our Balbriggan Rejuvenation Programme. The redevelopment 
of Quay Street and the Harbour area is due for completion this 
year while the creative hub planned for Dublin Street will 
welcome visitors from the end of next year. Locals and visitors 
to Balbriggan have witnessed the positive changes in the area 
in recent years as improvements take shape and there are 
exciting times ahead. There was further good news for the 
coastal town, and wider North Fingal area, with the approval 
of the planning for the Balbriggan Community Swimming Pool 
at last month’s council meeting. The investment of €11m in the 
project will cover the construction of a six-lane 25m pool with 
changing facilities, viewing gallery, meeting spaces, reception 
area, staff offices and welfare spaces. The carefully designed 
and planned proposal was refined through the public 
consultation process to include a variable pool depth ranging 
from 1.10 metres to 1.80 metres. This will accommodate a 
wider range of users and support activities including learn to 
swim programmes, swimming training and general recreation. 
This highly anticipated facility will be fully accessible and 
will hugely compliment the suite of activities and amenities 
available in the area as well as supporting active and social 
lifestyles for service users.

including

I

From Malahide to Donabate now and the newly imagined

Fingal in the coming months, all of which can be found on the 
following website  
https://www.eventsinfingal.ie/events I hope you can take the 
opportunity 
to attend 
and 
enjoy 
some 
of 
these fantastic events.   
 
Finally, as the AGM of Fingal County Council takes place on 
Friday, June 12th, the term of office of Mayor Tom O’Leary and 
Deputy Mayor Gráinne Maguire draws to a close. Before the 
chains of office pass to the next Mayor and Deputy Mayor, I 
know you will join me in expressing gratitude to them both for 
their commitment and dedication to their work on behalf of 
their constituents over the last year. No doubt there have been 
many standout moments for 
the 
Mayor 
and 
Deputy 
Mayor since their election on June 13th, 2025, and I hope this 
last year has been a fulfilling, enjoyable and memorable one.  
Best wishes, 
AnnMarie Farrelly

TOURISM DEVELOPMENT 
Explore Fingal Food Markets 
Following a successful pilot season in 2025, Fingal 
County Council has launched the 2026 Explore Fingal 
Markets programme, marking the first rollout within the 
wider Explore Fingal brand family.  
 
Laura Duffy, Chair of Fingal Food Circle; The Mayor of Fingal, Cllr Tom 
O’Leary; Wiseman, owner of SA Braai at Explore Fingal Markets 
Malahide. 
Page 4 
The programme began with the weekly Saturday Explore 
Fingal Market Malahide on 2nd May, followed by the 
launch of the monthly Explore Fingal Market Swords in 
Swords Castle on 16th May. A pilot market is also 
planned for Millennium Park, Blanchardstown on 13th 
June. 
 
Markets will run throughout the summer across 
Malahide, Swords and Blanchardstown, with a strong 
focus on local food producers, Fingal Food Circle 
members and Fingal farmers. All markets are free to 
attend and aim to support local enterprise while 
enhancing the visitor experience across Fingal.

Fingal County Council continued the rollout of the new 
Explore Fingal destination tourism brand through a 
series of regional brand workshops held in Malahide 
and Naul on 20th May, followed by Blanchardstown on 
21st May. The practical workshops were designed to 
support tourism, food and drink businesses in 
understanding the Explore Fingal brand and how it can 
be incorporated into their own marketing activity. 
Businesses were introduced to the brand guidelines, 
provided with access to downloadable assets and shown 
how alignment with the destination brand can support 
promotion, visibility and visitor engagement across the 
county.

The team also continues to support growing community 
involvement in tourism development through the 
delivery of Community Tourism Group Training held at 
Swords Carnegie Library on 13th May. Groups from 
Blanchardstown, Castleknock, Clonsilla, Swords, Naul, 
Donabate, and Malahide attended & this forms part of 
ongoing efforts to strengthen local engagement and 
community participation within Fingal’s tourism sector.

Preventing Homelessness, Notices to Quit and 
Tenant In-situ Acquisitions  
 
Fingal County Council is aware that households in the 
Fingal area who may have received a notice to quit,

which is also referred to as a notice of termination, from 
their landlord may be worried or unsure of what to 
do.  Fingal County Council and the Dublin Regional 
Homeless Executive (DRHE) would like to advise anyone 
affected of the services that are available to them in 
these circumstances.  
 
We strongly encourage tenants residing in the 
Fingal area, who have been issued with a notice 
of termination, to contact Fingal County Council 
as soon as they receive a notice from their 
landlord. The contact details for Fingal County 
Council are provided at the bottom of this page.  
 
When the tenants contact Fingal County Council, staff in 
the Housing Department will take note of the 
termination date.  
 
The Council advises the tenant to refer the notice to 
Threshold, a service funded by the DRHE to provide a 
Tenancy Protection Service for private renters in the 
Dublin Region, including Fingal. Threshold can also be 
contacted directly on Freephone 1800 454 454 or via 
their website www.threshold.ie which contains more 
information and advice on the validity of your notice.  
 
The Council’s first response will be to try to prevent 
homelessness. This includes assessing the person’s 
position on the social housing list, providing advice on 
applying for Choice Based Lettings, and advising the 
person on the level of Housing Assistance Payment (HAP) 
they may be eligible to receive. 
  
Placement in emergency accommodation will be a last 
resort if no other alternative can be identified.   
 
Fingal County Council continues to liaise with other 
Dublin and neighboring local authorities to deal with 
tenancy issues that may require an inter-authority 
approach.

Whilst the Council will, in the context of current 
circumstances, adopt flexibility in dealing with potential 
acquisitions of properties with tenants in situ, any 
acquisition is subject to appropriate due diligence and 
checks before any commitment is made to acquire, 
including, for example, determining that a valid notice 
of termination is in place, the tenant has a social 
housing need, and the condition and valuation of the 
property.  
  
The Government has put forward options to allow 
tenants who are not eligible for social housing to remain 
in their homes, including schemes to support the 
purchase of homes and a Cost Rental in-situ Scheme. 
The Cost Rental Tenant-in-Situ Scheme is available for 
tenants who are not eligible for social housing and are 
at risk of homelessness. The DHLGH has advised that 
local authorities are to be the first point of contact for 
this scheme, but it is managed by the Housing Agency. 
Under the scheme, the Housing Agency can purchase a 
property and rent it to the tenant. Fingal County Council 
will undertake an initial assessment of the tenant’s 
circumstances and refer details to the Housing Agency 
for consideration, where the tenant is at risk of 
homelessness and the Cost Rental Tenant-in-Situ 
scheme applies. The Housing Agency will then contact 
the landlord about the purchase of the property.  
  
Where a tenant wishes to purchase their home from the 
landlord, local authorities can provide advice about the 
Local Authority Home Loan scheme. The Government is 
examining implementing a ‘right of first refusal’ for 
tenants to purchase their homes, as well as expanding 
the First Home shared equity scheme. The Council will be 
able to provide more information on these when 
available.  Works around preventing homelessness, 
assessing notices of termination, and responding to 
tenant and landlord in-situ queries are being led on by 
the Council’s Homelessness section, taking a tenant-
centred approach, supported by staff dedicated to 
dealing with tenant in-situ housing acquisitions.

and completed this year’s Exercise: Energise Her Moves 
Programme. The programme is designed for girls aged 
12–15 who are not currently participating in sport or 
physical activity. Activities can take place during 
lunchtime and/or after school, with participants 
encouraged to choose the activities themselves. The 
main highlight for participants this year was an active 
multi-sports day held in March at the National Indoor 
Athletics Arena. 
A total of 429 participants took part across their schools, 
engaging in a wide range of activities including self-
defence, personal training, gym-work, dance, and 
cheerleading. Now in its 14th year, the programme 
continues to grow in popularity among both students 
and teachers. Pictured are students from Ardgillan
